digest.intro: AI proves math, cracks its own proof checker, and a fly outwits both.

items.title: How fruit flies navigate invisible smell ribbons
items.blurb: The old 'surge and cast' reflex model turns out to be wrong: Rockefeller's Vanessa Ruta showed that fruit flies build a spatial directional memory from each edge-crossing of an odor plume — essentially triangulating source direction across stuttered, chaotic chemical hits in turbulent air. The experiment required a custom fly treadmill to control what the animal was actually smelling moment to moment, because odor plumes are invisible and the method had made the problem intractable for decades. The upshot is a previously unknown navigation algorithm running on a brain the size of a pinhead, with direct implications for how drone swarms could search without GPS.

items.title: The Euler Disc is the wrong shape
items.blurb: The Euler disc problem — a spinning disc that rattles to a halt in finite time, which classical mechanics can't cleanly explain — gets a 'wait, actually' twist: the disc itself is the wrong shape for the phenomenon it's meant to demonstrate. Steve Mould is one of the best physics communicators working right now, and his videos reliably end with you wanting to go find something round and spin it on a surface.

items.title: Cycloidal gearbox, built from scratch by a 15-year-old
items.blurb: Three versions deep — the first two failed — before a working NEMA 17-footprint cycloidal drive at 1:9 ratio, plus a parametric Python generator for Fusion 360 so anyone can re-derive the geometry from the underlying equations. Cycloidal gearboxes are genuinely beautiful: nearly zero backlash, high torque density, and a motion profile that looks almost biological. The HN thread surfaced that 'wannabe engineer' in the repo title isn't false modesty — it's a legal/regulatory classification that creates real barriers for young makers.

sections.heading: The math-as-infrastructure story, cracking in real time

items.title: Mathematics without mathematicians
items.blurb: Written in direct response to OpenAI solving ten open mathematics problems, this essay systematically dismantles the coping mechanisms — 'we'll direct the AIs,' 'we'll teach what they discover,' 'we'll canonize the results' — and argues each one collapses under the same pressure: AI will eventually exceed humans at taste and intuition, not just computation. The most uncomfortable point isn't about math at all; the author notes the arguments are 'somewhat portable — replace mathematics with botany or whatever as needed.'

items.title: Postmortem: the Lean kernel soundness bug that briefly 'disproved' Collatz
items.blurb: On July 25, a sorry-free 'disproof' of the Collatz conjecture appeared — produced with AI assistance and passing the external Rust-based checker nanoda — before anyone realized it exploited a kernel bug in Lean's handling of phantom parameters in nested inductive types. The fix took one hour after the bug was formally reported, but the episode is sobering context for the AI math announcements: the trust layer beneath formal proofs is itself software, and it cracked. De Moura is the creator of Lean, so this is as primary as it gets.

items.title: Adelene Koh's bookbinding sculptures
items.blurb: Koh went unreasonably deep on one structural element — the sewn endband, the thread that quietly locks a book's spine — and turned invisible infrastructure into the subject of Loewe Craft Prize-shortlisted sculpture. Her piece 'Endless' is an ouroboros cylinder of meticulously folded paper stitched with 18th-century English endband technique, fore-edge bound to spine in an infinite loop. 'I'm drawn to the overlooked, the sidelined, the parts that quietly support everything else' is a sentence that describes a whole design philosophy.

items.title: Defcon's badge is a transparent security key you can see inside
items.blurb: Andrew 'bunnie' Huang designed this year's Defcon badge around the Baochip-1x — a three-years-in-the-making, mostly open-source microcontroller — with a transparent removable core module that functions as a standalone hardware security token after the conference. The transparency isn't cosmetic: it's a material statement that trust in hardware should be legible, auditable, and physically inspectable. The badge has a second life; the chip is the argument.

items.title: Three converging flashpoints: Iran, US-China trade, European instability
items.blurb: August enters with three structurally linked risk stories: Iran deal trajectory (fragile, oil-price-sensitive), US-China tariff escalation that has now structurally altered supply chain assumptions rather than just introducing volatility, and European banking supervisors formally flagging geopolitical risk as a material contributor to policy uncertainty across the continent. The useful frame here is that these are no longer episodic shocks — they've been priced in as permanent features of the landscape, which changes how markets and institutions respond to each new development.

items.title: The open-weights AI letter and what it's actually arguing
items.blurb: Willison synthesizes the past few weeks of competing open letters on AI development: the Microsoft-shepherded 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership' (235 signatories including NVIDIA, Amazon, YC, and eventually OpenAI) is explicitly designed to preempt government bans on open-weight models by framing closed models as the actual single-point-of-failure risk. The surprising inclusion is explicit support for distillation — training on other models' outputs — which is the live legal and technical battleground. Anthropic's counter-position is also in the thread.

facts.fact: A fruit fly's odor-navigation algorithm isn't a hardwired reflex — it builds a spatial directional memory across multiple plume edge-crossings, a mechanism only discovered after scientists built a treadmill to control exactly what the fly was smelling in real time.

A sorry-free 'disproof' of the Collatz conjecture circulated for days in July 2026 — produced with AI assistance and passing an independent Rust-based proof checker — before anyone identified that it exploited a soundness bug in Lean's kernel involving phantom parameters in nested inductive types.

Defcon's 2026 badge contains the Baochip-1x, an open-source microcontroller three years in development by Andrew 'bunnie' Huang, with a transparent removable core that functions as a standalone hardware security token — the badge has a designed second life after the conference.

A 15-year-old's parametric Python script generates cycloidal gearbox geometry for Fusion 360 from first principles — his first two physical versions failed due to tolerance limits in 3D printing before version three ran successfully on a NEMA 17 motor.

Adelene Koh's Loewe Craft Prize-shortlisted sculpture 'Endless' is structurally an ouroboros — a book's spine and fore-edge bound together in an infinite loop using 18th-century English endband sewing technique, making visible a structural element normally hidden inside a book's cover.

art_picks.title: Decalogue
art_picks.creator: Krzysztof Kieślowski
art_picks.why: Ten hour-long films organized around the Ten Commandments, but really a systems-thinker's study of how moral rules collide with lived human behavior — each episode a self-contained feedback loop where a tiny deviation cascades into irreversible consequence. The kind of thing that makes you want to go re-examine every structure you've ever taken for granted.

art_picks.title: Superstudio: Life Without Objects
art_picks.creator: Superstudio
art_picks.why: The Italian radical design collective's grid-world utopias are the purest case of software-as-mythology in design history — a continuous surface that renders all objects, status, and production obsolete. Category-annihilating work that still reads as provocation; the physical/digital threshold they were drawing in 1969 is basically where you live now.

art_picks.title: Either/Or
art_picks.creator: Elliott Smith
art_picks.why: A record built from obsessive layering — lo-fi tape loops, doubled vocals, arrangements that feel skeletal but are actually load-bearing — where the intimacy is structural, not confessional. The craft underneath is as intricate as any generative system; it just sounds like someone whispering in a room.

events.name: Greater New York 2026 — closing weeks
events.venue: MoMA PS1, Long Island City, Queens
events.why: The quinquennial survey of 53 NYC-based artists — site-specific commissions, animation, scenography, painting — organized around surveillance, economic precarity, and shifting tech; admission is free and the show takes over the entire building, with the last window to see it before it closes August 17.

events.name: Whitney Biennial 2026 (82nd Edition) — final weeks
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, Meatpacking District
events.why: The Biennial closes August 23 — curated by Marcela Guerrero and Drew Sawyer, it's the rare year where the Whitney and PS1 surveys overlap for the first time since 2010, making this a genuine moment to compare two different readings of what's happening in American art right now.

events.name: Andrew Bird with Wordless Music Orchestra — 20th Anniversary of The Mysterious Production of Eggs
events.why: Bird performs the album in its entirety with a full orchestra for the first time ever — a record built entirely on elaborate loops, multi-tracked violin, and layered systems — free admission, outdoors, and the kind of unreasonably committed performance that rewards obsessive craft.

events.name: AIGA NY × Museum of Arts and Design: Bring What You Love. Leave With Something New.
events.venue: Museum of Arts and Design (MAD), Columbus Circle
events.why: A design community swap-and-share evening hosted at MAD — intimate, practitioner-facing, and the kind of frontier social format where scenes are visible before they institutionalize; through August 16 at the museum for the wider context.

events.name: Taiwanese Waves 10th Anniversary: 9m88 + ØZI + YELLOW / Mong Tong / Chinatown Records
events.why: A showcase of contemporary Taiwanese pop, electronic, and experimental music marking the 10th anniversary of Taiwanese Waves — Mong Tong in particular blurs psychedelic folk with Taoist imagery and tape collage in a way that belongs squarely at the edge of culture becoming visible before it hardens; free.
